questions.text: Suppose that a shop has an equal number of LED bulbs of two different types. The probability of an LED bulb lasting more than 100 hours given that it is of Type 1 is 0.7, and given that it is of Type 2 is 0.4. The probability that an LED bulb chosen uniformly at random lasts more than 100 hours is _________.
questions.solution:
Both types are equally likely (0.5 each). Total probability:
[latex]P=0.5\times0.7+0.5\times0.4=0.35+0.2=0.55[/latex]

Answer: 0.55

questions.text: The minimum number of colours that is sufficient to vertex-colour any planar graph is _________.
questions.solution:
By the four colour theorem, every planar graph can be properly coloured with 4 colours, and some (e.g. [latex]K_4[/latex]) need all 4.

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider the following expressions:
(i) false
(ii) Q
(iii) true
(iv) [latex]P\vee Q[/latex]
(v) [latex]\neg Q \vee P[/latex]
The number of expressions given above that are logically implied by [latex]P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)[/latex] is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]P\wedge(P\Rightarrow Q)[/latex] means P is true and Q is true. Check each expression with P = Q = true:
- false False
- Q True, true True, [latex]P\vee Q[/latex] True, [latex]\neg Q\vee P[/latex] True

4 expressions are implied.

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider the following experiment.
Step 1. Flip a fair coin twice.
Step 2. If the outcomes are(TAILS, HEADS) then output Y and stop.
Step 3. If the outcomes are either(HEADS, HEADS) or(HEADS, TAILS), then output N and stop.
Step 4. If the out comes are(TAILS, TAILS), then go to Step1.
The probability that the output of the experiment is Y is (up to two decimal places)_____.
questions.solution:
In each round of two flips: Y with probability 1/4 (TH), N with 1/2 (HH or HT), repeat with 1/4 (TT).

[latex]P(Y)=\frac{1/4}{1/4+1/2}=\frac13\approx0.33[/latex]

Answer: 0.33

questions.text:
A function [latex]f:\mathbb{N}^{+}\rightarrow \mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], defined on the set of positive integers [latex]\mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], satisfies the following properties:
f(n)=f(n/2) if n is even
f(n)=f(n+5) if n is odd
Let R={[latex]i|\exists j:f(j)=i[/latex]} be the set of distinct values that f takes. The maximum possible size of R is ____.
questions.solution:
Both rules keep a number inside its class:
- If n is a multiple of 5, n/2 (when even) and n + 5 are still multiples of 5.
- If n is not a multiple of 5, neither are n/2 and n + 5.

Within each class all values are linked (e.g. 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, and 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5), so f can take at most one value per class: at most 2 values.

Answer: 2
